cards.text: This song comes from Asaph, the head musician King David appointed to serve before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:4-5). It's even got the tune written on top for the choirmaster: "Do Not Destroy." Then the whole crowd opens up: "We give thanks to You, O God"!

cards.question: The crowd says "we give thanks" twice in one breath. What reason do they give God?

answers.text: Because the harvest came in full

cards.text: Then a new voice comes in, speaking as I, and friend, that voice is God. Asaph's choir sings the opening and God takes the next verse. Talk about a GUEST FEATURE.

cards.question: God says a time of judging is coming. Who decides when it happens?

answers.text: The people pick it by praying
The enemy sets it by going too far

cards.question: When God judges, He says He will judge ___.

cards.text: Now God paints a picture. The earth and everybody living on it start to quake.

cards.question: With the whole earth quaking, who does God say bears up its pillars?

cards.text: Then comes a Selah, so let that land: the planet's shaking and God is holding it up. Meanwhile I need my ENTIRE mustache just to carry one cookie box across the bakery.

cards.question: Next God speaks to the proud. What does He tell them to stop doing?

cards.text: Then God tells the wicked not to lift up their horn, or speak with an outstretched neck. You know that neck: chin up, nose up, like the guy who just got promoted to assistant shift manager and needs the whole parking lot to know.

cards.question: God warns the wicked not to lift up their horn. Against what are they lifting it?

cards.text: Now the song explains why all that strutting goes nowhere. Exaltation doesn't come from the east or the west, and not out of the desert either.

cards.question: If exaltation doesn't come from the east, the west or the desert, where does it come from?
As the judge, God brings ___ one and ___ another.

cards.text: Then the song shows us a cup in the hand of the LORD. It's full of foaming wine mixed with spices, and the LORD pours from it.

cards.question: The LORD pours from His cup. Who drinks it?

answers.text: All the wicked of the earth
Only the kings of the nations

cards.question: The wicked take one sip from the LORD's cup and set it back down.
After the cup, the psalmist turns to himself: "But I…" What does he say he'll do?

cards.text: And the last line goes back to horns. Remember the wicked lifting theirs up with that outstretched neck, chin pointed at the ceiling?

cards.question: How does the song end for the horns of the wicked and the horns of the righteous?

answers.text: Wicked horns cut off and righteous horns exalted
Wicked horns exalted and righteous horns cut off
Both kinds of horns cut off alike

findings.problem: Card 1 cites Psalm 75:1, but no card tells its last line, 'The people declare Your wondrous works.' It is the only place the psalm says what the people do in response, and the baker never hears it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'Talk about a GUEST FEATURE' makes God the punchline by casting Him as a guest feature on someone else's song. The joke lands on God rather than on Papa Dorin or a human situation.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: 'Asaph's choir sings the opening' says who the 'We' of verse 1 is. The text leaves the 'We' open, and the heading only says the psalm is 'For the choirmaster.' Cards 1 and 2 do the same with 'the whole crowd' and 'The crowd.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Verse 3 is conditional: 'When the earth and all its dwellers quake.' The card turns it into an event that is happening: 'The earth and everybody living on it start to quake.' Card 7 ('With the whole earth quaking') and card 8 ('the planet's shaking') build on the same reading. The card should keep the 'when' framing.
Apart from naming the Selah, this card repeats what cards 6 and 7 already covered ('the planet's shaking and God is holding it up'). It does not move the passage forward.
The joke laughs at a made-up third person, 'the guy who just got promoted to assistant shift manager.' It also reads as mocking a modest promotion. Papa Dorin should be the one laughed at.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself.
